result:
The proposed answer of 10 is wrong because it omits 7.

PSL(2,8) (order 504) is a finite non-solvable group. Its irreducible character degrees are 1, 7, 7, 7, 7, 8, 9, 9, 9, which I checked via the sum of squares: 1 + 4·49 + 64 + 3·81 = 504. Every non-linear degree (7, 8, 9) has exactly one distinct prime divisor, so PSL(2,8) ∈ 𝒢. Therefore 7 ∈ P, and P ⊇ {2, 3, 5, 7}. The proposed solution's claim that A₅ is the unique such group is false.

VERDICT: REJECT
CONFIDENCE: 5
